Not exactly sure when this policy went into effect, but Google just fooled anyone who thought they were done with "being evil" when they de-linked YouTube from G-minus. Surprise! As though you thought there wouldn't still be hoops to jump through and Faustian bargains to be made if you want to comment on videos or (and this, I think, is the more important point) offer your own videos and contributions on the world's #1 video sharing and influencer site (like RamzPaul, Friendly Atheist, etc.).

Google joins Yahoo, AOL, Microsoft/MSN/Live/Bing/Outlook (whatever Sybil personality they're on now), and social media titans Facebook and Twitter in requiring what's called two-step verification. They claim, of course, that it's to minimize "abuse" -- both by spammers signing up for accounts en masse, and of course, the Sarkisian definition of "trolls" who need to be kept in line and held accountable for their nefarious speech by limiting how many accounts they can make (thus decreasing the overall anonymity of them).

As you can't sign up for a Google account at all without providing your phone number for "verification," you cannot sign up for Docs, Apps, Gmail, Play, or even Blogspot unless you give them either a mobile number or a landline that they can use to send an automated voice message containing your "one-time-use" security code. But... this means, of course, that they now have that number in their records and can use it however they please, without your knowledge. You, of course, implicitly consent to them doing this by your agreement to use their products -- or should I say, letting them use you as a product.

This is just another move by tech companies and their government overlords at the NSA to police "deviant behavior" by offering a carrot on a stick in exchange for your life story. After all, who in 2015 not only doesn't have a cell phone, but doesn't want to share it with anyone? The move further marginalizes those who still want to have a voice in what is the last dying vestige of democratic speech and even just casual discourse (the Internet) without handing over their identities, because more and more of the major "mainstream" online media outlets now require a "big-name" email account to sign up to comment (domains like Yopmail and GuerrillaMail are blacklisted) -- just in case you might try to make a drive-by account and be a "troll" who they can't keep an eye on.

Huffington Post infamously did this in 2013 to much furor, by doing away with their native login system and replacing it with the Facebook API. The site became a ghost town, but they did not revert to the old system -- proving that these sites would rather stick with a scorched-earth policy that eliminates comments altogether, or dwindles them to a niche echo chamber, rather than accept the good and the bad with the ugly.

(Can you say Reddit? I knew you could.)

So, good luck to anyone who wants to open a YouTube account or a Gmail, even if it's just a disposable Gmail to comment on some other website that doesn't play nice with true "throwaway" domains like 10 Minute Mail and doesn't use Disqus. Unless you play by their rules, you're on the outside looking in.
